CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, headache frequency, and sleep quality.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for a follow-up appointment approximately four weeks after his last visit. He reports that his anxiety symptoms have remained stable with continued use of Escitalopram at 20 mg daily. He has been practicing mindfulness techniques regularly, which he finds helpful during stressful periods. However, he expresses some concern regarding his persistent fatigue, which he attributes to ongoing sleep disturbances.
Mr. Smith notes that he has been using the CPAP machine as directed, and while he reports some improvement in sleep quality, he still experiences excessive daytime sleepiness and fatigue. He has been diligent about sleep hygiene practices but feels that the quality of his sleep is not adequate.
Regarding his tension-type headaches, Mr. Smith reports that since initiating Amitriptyline at 10 mg nightly, he has experienced a decrease in the frequency of headaches, now averaging three to four episodes per week. The severity of the headaches has also diminished, though he still occasionally resorts to Ibuprofen for symptomatic relief. He reports no significant side effects from the Amitriptyline.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General: Persistent fatigue; no significant weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Cardiovascular: Intermittent palpitations stable; denies chest pain or edema. Respiratory: No shortness of breath; CPAP compliance reported, no cough or wheezing. Gastrointestinal: Mild nausea persists; occasional bloating; no vomiting or changes in bowel habits. Neurological: Decreased frequency of tension headaches; no focal neurological deficits.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- Mild obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed on sleep study. - Tension-type headaches.
FAMILY HISTORY
- Father: Coronary artery disease, underwent CABG at age 60. - Mother: Hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
- Lives alone in , . Works as a teacher. No tobacco use; social alcohol consumption. No illicit drug use.
MEDICATIONS
- Atorvastatin 10 mg daily. - Magnesium supplement 400 mg daily. - Melatonin 3 mg nightly. - Escitalopram 20 mg daily. - Trazodone 50 mg nightly. - Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly. - CPAP machine for sleep apnea.
ALLERGIES
- No known drug allergies.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
VITALS: T 98.6F, HR 74 bpm, BP 120/76 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, O2 sat 96% on room air.
General: Well-nourished, alert, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. No peripheral edema. Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally; CPAP device noted, no wheezing or crackles. Gastrointestinal: Soft, non-tender abdomen; no epigastric tenderness. Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no focal deficits. No tenderness on palpation of the bilateral temporalis region.
LABORATORY DATA
Lipid Panel (obtained at last visit): Total Cholesterol 172 mg/dL, LDL 90 mg/dL, HDL 60 mg/dL, Triglycerides 95 mg/dL CBC: Normal BMP: Normal TSH: Normal
RADIOLOGICAL STUDIES
- No new studies indicated at this visit.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Persistent fatigue and sleep disturbances with ongoing anxiety. - Mr. Smith reports that while he has seen some improvement in sleep quality with CPAP usage, fatigue remains a concern. Continue Escitalopram at 20 mg daily. Maintain Trazodone at 50 mg nightly for sleep. Reassess CPAP usage and adherence at the next visit. Encourage Mr. Smith to continue practicing sleep hygiene and regular exercise. Follow up in 4 weeks to evaluate anxiety symptoms and overall fatigue.
2. Improved frequency of tension-type headaches. - The patient has noted a decrease in headache frequency since starting Amitriptyline. Continue Amitriptyline at 10 mg nightly and monitor for any potential side effects. Schedule follow-up in 4 weeks to assess headache frequency and severity.
3. Lipid management. - Continue Atorvastatin 10 mg daily due to stable lipid levels. Reassess lipid panel in 3 months to evaluate ongoing effectiveness.
4. Follow-up. - Schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks to reassess anxiety symptoms, sleep quality, headache frequency, and overall well-being. Encourage Mr. Smith to maintain a symptom diary to better identify patterns related to his fatigue and headaches. Discuss the importance of regular physical activity to enhance both physical and mental health.
